Reported Spill Volume: 30 gallons
Report Description
****WEB REPORT**** AT APPROXIMATELY 3:35AM AND TRACTOR/TRAILER WAS TRAVELING EAST BOUND ON INTERSTATE 80 NEAR COLFAX, CA WHEN THE DRIVER HIT A DEER. THE DEER PUNCTURED THE SADDLE TANK AND DIESEL FUEL BEGAN TO LEAK FOR FOUR MILES UNTIL THE DRIVER COULD EXIT THE INTERSTATE IN THE TOWN OF COLFAX, CA. IT IS ESTIMATED 25 GALLONS LEAKED DURING THIS TIME. THE TRUCK PARKED ON THE OFF RAMP WHERE THERE WAS A SMALL AMOUNT OF PRODUCT AND THEN THE DRIVER MOVED THE VEHICLE TO AN ADJACENT PAVED PARKING LOT WHERE THERE WAS ABOUT 3 - 4 GALLONS OF DIESEL ON THE PAVED LOT. THE DRIVER CALLED 911 AND THE CHP AND CALTRANS WAS DISPATCHED TO THE SCENE TO CONTAIN THE SPILL. CALTRANS WILL ADDRESS ANY PRODUCT ON THE INTERSTATE AND TOW COMPANY/CONTRACTOR WILL TAKE CARE OF PRODUCT AT THE VEHICLE LOCATION.

properties.summary: Incident Type: UNKNOWN SHEEN - NRC Report ID: 978540 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: SWEPCO KNOX LEE POWER PLANT
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 978540
Incident Time: 2011-06-03 11:20:00
Nearest City: Longview, TX
Incident Type: UNKNOWN SHEEN
Material: UNKNOWN OIL
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: SWEPCO KNOX LEE POWER PLANT
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Sheen Size: 3 feet by 1 feet (area 3 sq. ft.)
Reported Spill Volume: 15 gallons
Skytruth Minimum Possible Spill Volume: 0 gallons
ON JUNE 3, 2011 AT APPROXIMATELY 2:30 AM OPERATIONS PLACED UNIT 5'S WEST TURBINE OIL COOLER IN SERVICE IN ORDER TO CONTROL OIL TEMPERATURE. AT APPROXIMATELY 6:20 AM, A PUMPER (OPERATOR) MAKING HIS ROUNDS OBSERVED A SHEEN ON THE ECOLOGY PIT. AT THIS TIME, HE NOTIFIED THE LEAD OPERATOR WHO IN TURN, NOTIFIED THE PLANTS QUALIFIED INDIVIDUAL (QI) WHO IMMEDIATELY WENT TO THE LOCATION AND PLACED TYGON TUBING INTO THE PIT AND REALIZED THAT IT WAS OIL. THE QI AT THAT TIME WENT TO GET MICRO BLAZE AND PUMPER BEGAN SPRAYING THE PIT WHILE THE QI PLACED BOOMS INTO IT. WHILE THIS WAS GOING ON, THE QI ASKED ANOTHER OPERATOR TO GO THROUGHOUT THE PLANT AND LOOK AT ALL SUMP PITS IN ORDER TO DETERMINE IF A SHEEN IS VISIBLE (NONE NOTICED). CLEAN UP WAS ASSISTED BY OTHER OPERATORS AND MAINTENANCE INDIVIDUALS WHO CAME OUT AND PLACED OTHER MULTIPLE OIL SOAK PADS AND MORE BOOMS. THE QI, AND ANOTHER SUPERVISOR SHUT OFF SUSPECTED OIL LEAK SOURCE. AFTER THE ECOLOGY PIT OIL WAS UNDER SOME CONTROL, THE PLANT ENVIRONMENTAL COORDINATOR WENT DOWN THE DISCHARGE CANAL TO SEE IF THERE WAS A VISIBLE SHEEN; ONLY MINUTE TRACES WERE SEEN AFTER THE PLANT'S 1ST BOOM, AND NONE WAS SEEN AFTER THE PLANT'S 2ND BOOM.
